$comment: The Sealed Crate in the Crate Yard (docs/specs/ISLAND-05-sunspire-sands.md §5.2): the caravan row’s board (Customize, Browse, the Plugins filter, the marketplace), the bill of lading (the plugin’s details and repository), the scale (Install, the Installed tab), the bell (/skills reload and the / menu), and Samir’s bench (the prompt’s limits and the check of the skill’s work). The places and lamps are the game’s; every word is this file’s.

text.title: The Sealed Crate
text.intro: Find the crate, read what’s inside, take it in, call for its skill, and check its work.

laps.title: The Sealed Crate: one small CSS proposal

stations.title: Find the plugin
stations.prompt: You search **Browse** for `modern-web-guidance` and nothing shows. What now?

options.text: Select **Add** > **Manage marketplaces…** and confirm that **awesome-copilot** is in the **Marketplaces** list
options.result: The caravan’s row is on the list. The crate shows on the board.

options.text: Install another plugin with a name like it
options.reason: Use `modern-web-guidance` for this exercise. If it can’t be had, record the exercise as blocked rather than installing an unrelated plugin.

options.text: Change your company’s managed settings to allow it
options.reason: Do not change company-managed settings to complete the exercise. Read the example, record it as blocked, and continue.

hints: A marketplace is a catalog of plugins.

stations.title: Review what’s inside
stations.prompt: The crate is on the board, sealed. What do you do before **Install**?

options.text: Open its details and review the description, then compare them with the plugin’s repository
options.result: The lading matches the maker’s mark: `GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance`. Its skill uses `npx` to run a documentation tool.

options.text: Install it. The marketplace’s description is enough
options.reason: Read its contents, not only the marketplace description. Some plugins start processes, call services, or run hooks.

options.text: Install it. The maker is well known
options.reason: A known maker still ships contents you review: the skill instructions, and any command approval before use.

hints: What does the board’s label leave out?
The details don’t show the source.
Open the details, then compare them with the plugin’s repository.

stations.title: Install it
stations.prompt: You’ve read the lading. The scale takes the crate in.
stations.text: The crate goes on the scale and into the yard. On **Installed** it shows under **Plugins**, with its enabled toggle on. Nothing inside it has run.

stations.title: Invoke its skill
stations.prompt: The plugin is installed. How do you put its skill to work?

options.text: Submit `/skills reload`, type `/`, select the `modern-web-guidance` skill, then add the prompt
options.result: The bell rings and the skill answers to its name. Its command can carry a plugin prefix.

options.text: Nothing more: it’s installed, so it’s working
options.reason: Installation alone doesn’t prove that the skill ran. You still invoke it.

options.text: Close the window and open it again
options.reason: Run `/skills reload` first. And closing a window isn’t the same as quitting the app.

hints: What does the bell plate say?
`/skills reload`, then `/` and the skill by name.

stations.title: Word the order
stations.prompt: Samir chalks the order for the skill. Which lines keep it small and safe?

tiles.text: Use only general terms in external queries
Propose at most one CSS-only improvement
Don’t add JavaScript, change files, or run app checks
If the plugin skill is unavailable, stop
Redesign the book cards while you’re there
tiles.reason: It’s one book-title layout question, not a redesign.
Inspect the files locally. External queries use only general terms.

stations.title: Check its work
stations.prompt: The skill proposes `text-wrap: balance` for long book titles. What do you check?

options.text: The skill activity and its guide-search output, that it names the real title element and CSS, and what happens in browsers that don’t support it
options.result: It names the guide it used, the support, and a browser check. No Book App file changed.

options.text: Nothing: it came from an installed plugin
options.reason: You still inspect its tool activity and check its recommendation against the code.

options.text: Apply it and run the app checks
options.reason: This exercise proposes. It does not change files or run app checks.

hints: The activity, the guide, and the code it names.
Inspect the activity, and ask what happens where the browser doesn’t support it.
